rca of the issue: Root cause: /api/admin/overview iterated over tickets and executed `ticket.get('assigned_helper').get('id')`. For tickets that were never assigned to a helper, `assigned_helper` is stored as None (or missing), so `.get('id')` on None raised AttributeError -> HTTP 500. The Coordinateur user could authenticate correctly and current_admin passed, but the endpoint crashed before returning, giving the false impression that admin access was broken. Fix: replace with `(ticket.get('assigned_helper') or {}).get('id')` on admin.py:56 — coerces None/missing to {} and returns None from .get('id'), never matching a helper.id. Reproduction (before fix): (1) create a ticket without assigning a helper (assigned_helper=null), (2) call GET /api/admin/overview as Coordinateur, (3) observe 500 AttributeError in backend logs. Mitigation validated: with 1 unassigned ticket currently in prod (unassigned_tickets=1), the endpoint returns 200 and the helper loop enumerates all 6 helper rows cleanly. Complementary feature validated: DELETE /api/admin/tickets/{ticket_id} is now registered under router prefix /admin, guarded by current_admin, returns 204 on success and 404 on unknown ID; the front-end delete-ticket-button is admin-gated and calls the correct endpoint after window.confirm.
